Question Choices: About what percent of normally distributed data lie within 3 standard deviations of the mean?
Hints: Use the third part of the empirical rule.;Recall 68-95-99.7.
Solution: For a normal distribution, the empirical rule places approximately 68%, 95% and 99.7% within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations, respectively. Thus within 3 standard deviations on either side of the mean is about 99.7%. These are approximations, not universal percentages for all distributions.

Question Choices: Assume a normal distribution. Scores have mean 80 and standard deviation 4. Between which two scores do about 95% of students fall? Enter the lower then upper value.
Hints: Go two standard deviations each way.;80 - 8 and 80 + 8.
Solution: The interval is mean plus or minus 2 standard deviations: 80-2(4)=72 and 80+2(4)=88. Enter the lower endpoint then the upper endpoint. Under the stated normal model this contains about 95% of values.

Question Choices: In a normal distribution, what percent of data lie above the mean?
Hints: The distribution is symmetric.;Half the data lie on each side.
Solution: A normal distribution is symmetric about its mean and has total area 1. Each half has area 1/2, so 50% lies above the mean. A single point at the mean has zero probability in this continuous model.

Question Choices: A data value equals the mean of a normal distribution. What is its z-score?
Hints: z = (value - mean)/standard deviation.;The numerator is zero.
Solution: At the mean, value-mean=0. Dividing by the positive standard deviation gives z=0.

Question Choices: Scores have mean 100 and standard deviation 15. What is the z-score of a value of 130?
Solution: Subtract the mean and divide by the positive standard deviation: z=(130-100)/15=30/15=2. The value is two standard deviations above the mean.
